portInfo.description: Parikia’s church complex, archaeological museum and castle hill give the port town a substantive identity. Naoussa is a separate village and Lefkes an inland one; neither belongs in a supposedly walkable Parikia itinerary. The island’s marble history is useful context, not a reason to fill a day with unsourced quarry access.

thingsToDo.intro: Pick one neighbourhood or excursion scale and keep time for the gangway queue on the way back.
topThings: Panagia Ekatontapiliani — Ekatontapiliani church complex, Parikia, Paros. An active early-Christian monument; worship controls interior access. Allow 50 minutes; official source.
Archaeological Museum of Paros — Archaeological Museum, Parikia, Paros. A distinct collection of island archaeology; verify current opening. Allow 75 minutes; official source.
Kastro of Parikia — Kastro hill, Parikia old settlement. Castle remnants reuse ancient architectural pieces; expect uneven lanes. Allow 45 minutes; official source.
Ancient Cemetery — Ancient cemetery site, Parikia, Paros. A different archaeological site, not the museum entrance; check viewing/access. Allow 30 minutes; official source.
Naoussa — Naoussa village centre, Paros. A road excursion to another village, not a walk from the tender. Allow 75 minutes; official source.
thingsToDo.shortCall: Stay near the port area and keep a generous buffer before all-aboard.
thingsToDo.standardCall: Combine a central walk, one attraction, and lunch if times allow—start back well before all-aboard.
thingsToDo.longerCall: A second stop or coach outing is realistic only with confirmed transport and an eight-hour or longer window.
thingsToDo.practicalTip: Label a boat ticket by its departure port. Parikia–Antiparos and Pounta–Antiparos are different journeys; neither is assumed available or safe within this tender day.

gettingThere.distanceToCity: Budget 45 minutes for the ship-to-confirmed-Parikia landing/queue and the same for return. Once there, the church/museum/Kastro circuit is a town walk; inland or Naoussa excursions need a retained vehicle. The authority describes a seasonal Parikia–Antiparos passenger crossing of about an hour; it must not be confused with a much shorter Pounta ferry crossing or sold as a verified cruise-day connection.
